description: Conan Surfaces — T3-parity right panel beside the chat: Browser / Terminal / Files / Diff as internal windows, 2-up side-by-side max (v1), per-thread. Source PRD: prd-conan-surfaces.md (READ IT FIRST every iteration — it carries the T3 reference mandate, the reuse map of dormant terminal-era code, and Randy's ratified decisions: 2-up v1; closing a Terminal window KILLS its shell). Read CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md first. House rules: semantic theme tokens only (post-retheme: shadcn neutral, monochrome primary), shadcn primitives, h-9 shrink-0 panel toolbars, capability-driven (no provider branching), CORS reflector + WS Origin allowlist on every new gateway endpoint. Gateway runs with `npm start` (NO watch — restart after ANY src/ edit; a stale gateway 404s new routes). Gates: `npm run typecheck` AND `npm test` AND `cd ui && npm run build`. Browser QA on the throwaway stack (CONAN_PORT=3799 CONAN_DATA_DIR=/tmp/x npm start + CONAN_PORT=3799 CONAN_UI_PORT=5199 npm run dev + CONAN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5199) — NEVER against dev :3747/:5173.

userStories.title: SurfacePanel shell: right panel + splitter + T3 'Open a surface' card grid
userStories.description: As a user, I want an 'Open' affordance on my thread that reveals a right panel with T3's surface picker, so chat and a workspace surface live side by side.
acceptanceCriteria: New `ui/src/components/SurfacePanel.tsx` mounted inside ChatPane's main row (right of the transcript column, inside the same flex row that holds the spine + transcript) — per-thread, so each mounted ChatPane owns its panel state
Toolbar entry: a 'Surfaces' (or panel icon) button in ThreadToolbar.tsx toggles the panel; panel is CLOSED by default

Open panel with no surface selected shows the T3-style empty state: centered 'Open a surface' heading, 'Choose what to show in the right panel.' subline, and a 2x2 card grid — Browser ('Open a local app or URL.'), Terminal ('Start a shell in this workspace.'), Files ('Browse and read workspace files.'), Diff ('Review changes in this thread.') — lucide icons, shadcn-card styling, semantic tokens only

Selecting any card mounts a stub surface window: h-9 shrink-0 header bar with the surface name + an X close button; closing returns to the card grid; stub body says the surface is coming in a later story

Panel width is draggable via a splitter handle on its left edge (pointer events, min 320px, max 60% of the pane); the transcript column flexes correctly and the F8 composer alignment is not regressed (the composer axis matches the transcript axis with the panel both open and closed)
Panel open/width state is per-thread in-memory (switching threads preserves each thread's panel state; no persistence yet)
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using the automate-browser skill on the throwaway stack: screenshot the card grid, a stub surface open, and the splitter at two widths, in BOTH light and dark
userStories.notes: Phase 0a. The T3 screenshot description in prd-conan-surfaces.md §benchmark is the layout contract. Keep the spine + transcript + panel in one flex row; the composer stays full-row below — check the F8 gutter still balances (the matching right gutter may need to collapse when the panel is open). Suggested skills: automate-browser, shadcn, build-ui.

userStories.title: 2-up internal windows: open a second surface side by side
userStories.description: As a user, I want two surfaces open at once (e.g. Files beside Diff), so I can reference one while reviewing the other.
acceptanceCriteria: With one surface open, a '+' affordance in the panel header (or an 'Open another surface' entry) shows the card grid for the SECOND window; the two internal windows split the panel 50/50 vertically (side by side), each with its own h-9 header + close
Max 2 windows (v1 decision) — with 2 open, the add affordance is hidden/disabled
Closing one window gives its space to the other; closing the last returns to the card grid; the same surface type may be open in both windows without state bleed
Per-thread in-memory state extends to both windows (type per slot)
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using the automate-browser skill: two stub surfaces side by side, close-one/close-both flows, light + dark screenshots
userStories.notes: Phase 0b. Depends on US-001. Randy ratified 2-up max for v1 — do not build n-window management. Suggested skills: automate-browser, shadcn.

userStories.title: Files surface: revive FileExplorer pegged to the thread's project cwd
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Files surface that browses my thread's workspace read-only, so I can inspect files without leaving the chat.
acceptanceCriteria: The Files card mounts the dormant `ui/src/components/FileExplorer.tsx` (adapted as needed) inside a surface window, rooted at the thread's project cwd (the same cwd ChatPane already receives) — directory tree + file content view, read-only, via the existing gateway fs routes ChatPane/PinPicker already use (GET /api/fs/read + the DirBrowser listing route); NO new gateway endpoints

Fix the known FileExplorer scrollbar drift while remounting (CLAUDE.md TODO): its scroll container must get the themed 6px scrollbar — root it in an <aside> like the transcript, or reuse FadeScroll — not the OS default scrollbar
Binary/huge files degrade gracefully (size-capped read with an honest 'too large / binary' notice rather than a hang or garbage render)
Surface header shows the cwd basename; h-9 shrink-0 per convention
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using the automate-browser skill: browse into a nested dir, open a text file, screenshot light + dark
userStories.notes: Phase 1a. Depends on US-001. Reuse map is in prd-conan-surfaces.md — FileExplorer.tsx is dormant but present; DirBrowser.tsx shows the listing-route usage. Suggested skills: automate-browser, build-ui.

userStories.title: Diff backend: POST /api/fs/diff — per-file working-tree git diffs
userStories.description: As the Diff surface, I need a gateway endpoint that returns working-tree git diffs for a set of paths, so the UI can render this thread's changes.
acceptanceCriteria: New gateway endpoint POST /api/fs/diff accepting {cwd, paths?: string[]} — runs git in the repo containing cwd and returns JSON: per-file {path, status (modified/added/deleted/untracked), patch (unified diff text, size-capped with a truncated flag)}; omit paths → all working-tree changes in that repo

Non-repo cwd returns {repo:false, files:[]} (200, honest empty) — never a 500; paths outside the repo root are rejected; the endpoint is auth-token'd and behind the CORS reflector like every /api route (src/gateway/index.ts conventions)
Pure diff-parsing/shaping logic lives in a testable module (src/fs/diff.ts or similar), not inline in the route handler
Unit tests: fixture repo (init in a tmpdir) covering modified + untracked + deleted, the non-repo case, and the size-cap truncation flag; node --test green
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Phase 1b backend — NO browser needed; ideal Codex story (sandboxed, unit-test-verifiable). Independent of US-001–003. Gateway restart note in the description applies when manually curling — tests drive the module directly. Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: Diff surface: review this thread's changes with the existing DiffView renderer
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Diff surface to show what this thread changed, so I can review the agent's work without leaving the chat.
acceptanceCriteria: The Diff card mounts a surface listing this thread's touched files: paths extracted client-side from the thread's transcript tool items (Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit inputs across history + live items — the same items ChatPane already renders), deduped, then hydrated via POST /api/fs/diff with the thread cwd
Per-file rows (path + status + +N/−N) expand to the unified diff rendered with the SAME red/green row treatment as ChatPane's DiffView (extract/reuse that renderer — do not fork a second diff style)
A refresh control re-fetches; an empty state says no changes when the thread touched nothing or the working tree is clean; truncated patches show the honest truncated notice
A thread whose touched files have since been committed shows the clean-tree empty state (v1 is working-tree-only — surface copy says 'Uncommitted changes')
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using the automate-browser skill: run a throwaway-stack thread that edits a file, open Diff, screenshot expanded diff light + dark
userStories.notes: Phase 1b UI. Depends on US-001 + US-004. DiffView lives in ChatPane.tsx (~line 1856) — extracting it to a shared component is in scope. Suggested skills: automate-browser, build-ui.

userStories.title: Terminal surface: revive the pty stack as a workspace shell (close = kill)
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Terminal surface running a real shell in my thread's workspace, so I can run commands beside the chat.
acceptanceCriteria: The Terminal card mounts an xterm.js terminal (reuse the dormant Terminal.tsx/@xterm wiring and getTerminalTheme()) connected to the gateway's /ws/terminal pty route with mode=shell and cwd = the thread's project path — verify the dormant route still registers on the gateway and revive it if it was unplugged

Closing the surface window KILLS the pty (Randy's ratified decision — no keep-alive, no background shells); switching threads (pane hidden, not unmounted) does NOT kill it; a dead/exited shell shows an honest 'shell exited' state with a restart affordance
Terminal theme derives from the active theme tokens (getTerminalTheme) and flips correctly with the sidebar light/dark toggle
The WS connection uses the existing auth/Origin-allowlist upgrade path — no new auth surface
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes

Verify in browser using the automate-browser skill: open Terminal, run `pwd` (output shows the thread cwd), close the window, verify via the gateway (e.g. GET /api/terminals or process check) that the pty is gone; screenshot light + dark
userStories.notes: Phase 2. Depends on US-001. The terminal-era footguns in CLAUDE.md apply (WS-close kills pty — here that is the DESIRED behavior on window close; ensure hidden-not-unmounted panes don't trigger it). Suggested skills: automate-browser, run.

userStories.title: Browser surface v1: local-app preview via iframe, honest about framing limits
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Browser surface to open my local dev apps (e.g. a Vite server) beside the chat, so I can watch the app I'm building without leaving Conan.
acceptanceCriteria: The Browser card mounts a surface with a URL bar (defaults to empty with placeholder suggesting http://localhost:…) + go/refresh controls in the h-9 header, rendering the target in an <iframe> body

Frame-refused targets (X-Frame-Options/CSP — most public sites) surface an honest error state explaining the v1 limitation ('This site refuses to be embedded — Browser v1 previews local apps') with an 'Open in system browser' fallback link; detection via iframe load failure/timeout heuristic, not silence
localhost/127.0.0.1 URLs render and navigate (history back/forward within the surface is NOT required v1); the URL bar reflects manual reloads
Per-window state: the entered URL survives switching threads (in-memory, same as panel state)

A short section is APPENDED to prd-conan-surfaces.md recording the v1 iframe decision and what the Tauri child-webview v2 would add (full-site browsing) — the spike's decision doc, kept where the mandate lives
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes

Verify in browser using the automate-browser skill: load the throwaway-stack UI's own URL (http://localhost:5199) inside the surface (Conan-in-Conan), screenshot; attempt https://github.com and screenshot the honest refusal state; light + dark
userStories.notes: Phase 3, scoped to the iframe path — the Tauri child-webview full browser is explicitly v2 (Rust work, stays out of the autonomous loop per prd-conan-surfaces.md). WKWebView CORS strictness gotcha does not apply to plain iframe embeds of localhost origins; packaged-app QA is NOT required for this story (dev-webview QA only). Suggested skills: automate-browser.
